name: Digital Realty
key_signal: DLR has broken below its 50-day moving average (185.7) and sits right at 200-day support (173.5) with negative MACD and RSI 39, while trading at a stretched 64x forward P/E despite only 5.7% ROE.
thesis: Data center demand tied to AI/cloud buildout continues to drive 16.7% revenue growth and 67.6% earnings growth, and DLR's pullback from its 52-week high of $208 to $173.88 puts it right at 200-day trend support with a golden cross still technically intact, offering a potential entry point for a sector leader with a 2.81% dividend and 31 analysts still rating it a buy.
bear_case: The stock's momentum has clearly deteriorated (-8.7% over 21 days, -12% over 63 days, MACD histogram deeply negative) and it just lost the 50-day moving average, suggesting institutional selling into what is already an expensive stock (46x trailing, 64x forward P/E, 2.68x book) whose ROE of only 5.7% signals the AI-driven capex boom is not yet translating into efficient returns on equity capital, all while debt/equity sits elevated at 76.6% in a market still sensitive to rate expectations for capital-intensive REITs — if 200-day support at ~173.5 fails, the next real floor is well below current price given the 52-week low of 146.23.
